scalars.scalar_value: A minimum of 5 years of general office experience with increasing responsibility in administrative and clerical assignments is required. Word processing experience is required. Experience with Workday finance/budget software is preferred . Experience working independently, taking initiative, and managing office functions is required, preferably at an academic institution.

The regular hours for this full-time position are 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday – Friday. Overtime, holiday, weekend and evening work hours may be required. Regular hours may vary due to needs of the College or division.

items.item_text: A minimum of 5 years of general office experience with increasing responsibility in administrative and clerical assignments is required. Word processing experience is required. Experience with Workday finance/budget software is preferred . Experience working independently, taking initiative, and managing office functions is required, preferably at an academic institution.
i. Collect and archive teaching evaluations; provide copies as needed for review.
i. Draft annual department/program budgets for Department Chairs’ and Program Coordinators’ approval and prepare and submit budget requests.
ii. Allocate and track budget expenditures, prepare quarterly budget reports for departments/programs and monthly purchasing card reports for the business office.
iii. Create and maintain Excel spreadsheets to track expenditures in department/program lecture series.
i. Research and compose correspondence, reports, and memos.

ii. Maintain inventory and check-out system for department/program-owned video and voice recorders, iPods, and transcribers for loan to students; maintain Hahn Building Lost & Found; post list in Digester -attempt to find owners of lost articles.
iii. Coordinate advertising; create targeted mailing lists.
iv. Arrange catering for receptions and meals for field trips, speakers, retreats, and department and public events, lecture series, and colloquia.
i. Advise Department Chairs/Program Coordinators, faculty, and students on College and department/program policies and guidelines.
ii. Investigate, evaluate, and resolve problems related to supervisory, administrative, and clerical responsibilities.
iii. Interact with students, answer inquiries or direct them to proper channels.
i. Update and submit department/program catalog and course descriptions annually; maintain records of new and revised courses; request appropriate course numbers.
ii. Prepare and submit department/program course schedules; request classroom assignments each semester.
iii. Prepare and maintain master calendar of Hahn classroom schedules.
iv. Arrange travel, lodging, meals, media services, venues, receptions, and honoraria for speakers in annual department lecture series.

i. Assist in faculty search and hiring process; submit job advertisements; prepare and submit search budget worksheets; track and report search expenses; acknowledge applications; maintain applicant files; contact short-listed candidates and schedule telephone interviews; create visiting candidates’ itineraries; schedule meetings and interview; arrange public lectures, receptions, transportation, lodging and meals; provide figures and statistics for faculty search reports.

ii. Provide administrative/clerical support for faculty promotion reviews: request evaluations from students; compile and mail dossiers to peer reviewers; assure confidentiality of review materials; compile dossiers for submission to President, Dean, and FPC.
i. Arrange for duplicating of syllabi, class handouts, reading packets, exams, and research materials.
ii. Arrange campus vehicle (Sagecoach) or rental van transportation for class field trips.
iii. Maintain college driver certification records for faculty who drive students to department events and field trips.

iv. Create and maintain email distribution lists for faculty, majors, student groups, affiliated departments (Chicano Studies, Asian-American Studies), and Sociology & Anthropology faculty at the other Claremont Colleges.
i. Locate vendors; purchase office equipment, supplies, teaching, and library materials.
i. Assist faculty in monitoring their research funding expenditures.
